`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

All notable changes to **HuntReplay Studio** are documented in this file.

## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-29

### Added
- **Favorites**: star a clip on its card or in the player. Stars are kept across restarts and renames, and a Favorites chip appears in the gallery once something is starred.
- **Filters**: chips for Kills, Downs and Multi-kills with counts; they combine with Favorites and the search.
- **Grid or list**: the clip list can switch between compact cards and thumbnail tiles.
- **Player**: skip back and forward 10 s, and full screen (F, Esc or a double-click to leave).
- **Graphics card details** on the dashboard: API, driver version and video memory.

### Changed
- The gallery shows the player beside the clip list, sized so the video fills the height. In a narrow window the list moves below the player.
- Clicking a clip only opens it in the player; the box on a card, Ctrl and Shift build the selection, so playing and selecting no longer get in each other's way. Arrow keys move through clips without selecting them.
- The selection bar below the gallery shows the count and total size, with Play selected (for one clip) and Delete.
- Clip cards show the event and the date and time; event badges are coloured (kills green, downs red, multi-kills blue).
- The gallery opens the newest clip on the first visit instead of an empty player.
- The dashboard banner has new artwork.
- Recent highlights on the dashboard keep the video's shape instead of being cropped into a strip, and a wider window shows more of them (up to six).
- Theme and language buttons moved to the bottom of the sidebar; the sidebar's Open clips folder link and the LOCAL label are gone (the gallery header still opens the folder).

---

## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-25

### Added
- **Select several clips**: tick the circle on a clip, or Ctrl- and Shift-click. Shift fills everything between the selected clips and the one you click; Ctrl+A selects all. Delete them with one confirmation: a clip that is open in another program is skipped and reported, the rest are deleted.
- **Selection mode**: with two or more clips selected, clicking a clip plays it without losing the selection. A bar next to the search box shows how many clips are selected, with Delete selected and Clear selection (or Esc).
- **Clip menu**: the ... button on a clip, a right-click or Shift+F10 opens Trim, Rename (F2), Show in Explorer, Open with system player and Delete (Del).

### Changed
- Redesigned clip cards: the preview fills the card with the event and length on it, and the title is the date and time, or your own name for a renamed clip. The play button, selection circle and menu appear when you point at a card.
- Keyboard in the gallery: arrows move between clips, Enter plays or pauses, Delete and F2 work on the selection.
- The buttons under the player act on the clip in the player, which its card marks "In player".
- Dashboard: the sidebar tagline is gone, recent highlights keep three columns, and the session log can be collapsed.
- Lower memory use when the library refreshes during a match.

### Fixed
- Saving a trimmed fragment over an existing clip and then cancelling, or hitting an error, deleted that clip. The file is now replaced only once the fragment is finished.
- If the Highlights connection was busy at startup or dropped later, Studio stopped receiving game events until restarted. It now reconnects.
- Cancelling a fragment export could break a newer one, which then could no longer be cancelled.
- Interrupted exports left hidden .partial.mp4 files in the clips folder; they are now cleaned up.
- Error messages could end with an old, unrelated FFmpeg warning.

---

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-18

### Added
- **In-place updates**: the header update button downloads the new HuntReplayStudio.exe from the latest GitHub release, verifies its SHA-256 digest, replaces the running executable and restarts. The download can be cancelled; any failure is explained with options to retry or open the releases page.
- **Support card** in the sidebar with a GitHub link and wallet addresses to copy.

### Changed
- Release notes in the update confirmation are shown as plain text, without raw links or Markdown.
- Gallery hides clip details until a clip is selected and trims long labels; ComboBox text trims instead of overflowing.

### Fixed
- Recordings could show teal or green bars around the picture: captured frames now fill the output instead of being letterboxed.
- A saved GPU is resolved by ID, name or legacy index, so Settings and the capture engine agree after upgrades or adapter reordering.
- Mouse wheel over the gallery clip list did not scroll the page.

---

## [0.1.9] - 2026-10-16

### Added
- **Notifications over the game** (Settings → System, off by default): a small click-through notice when a clip is saved, the replay buffer starts or stops, or recording fails. It never takes focus from the game and is never recorded into clips. Choice of corner and duration, with a preview button. Not shown while a game runs in exclusive fullscreen, where a window on top can freeze it; borderless and windowed modes show it.
- **More output resolutions**: 720p, 900p, 1080p, 1200p, 1440p, 1600p and 2160p. Each keeps the monitor's aspect ratio (1080p on a 3440 × 1440 monitor records 2580 × 1080 instead of letterboxing), and resolutions above the monitor's own are hidden. Existing 1080p / 1440p / 2160p settings carry over.
- **Language switch in the first-run setup wizard**.

### Changed
- A new install starts in the Windows display language (Russian or English).
- Default bitrate raised from 25 to 40 Mbit/s: Hunt is often very dark and low rates smear shadows. Existing settings keep their bitrate.
- Encoders use recording-oriented presets; frame pacing uses a high-resolution timer.
- Audio follows a change of the default Windows output device during recording.
- Trimming re-encodes on the GPU encoder when one is available; the built-in player decodes on the GPU and refreshes in step with the display.
- Lower memory churn while buffering; many internal performance and readability improvements.
- The NVIDIA container is paused only when it actually holds the Highlights pipe.

### Fixed
- The chosen language was lost after a restart when settings were saved later.
- Unsaved-settings question needed a second click before it switched pages.
- During a trimmed-fragment preview, the playback position could start slightly before the fragment.
- Player restart after the end of a clip could crash; portable mode registered trimmed clips in the wrong library; clip folders on network shares failed exports; QSV keyframes; several smaller audit fixes.

---

## [0.1.6] - 2026-10-11

### Added
- **Interactive Video Trimming in Gallery**:
  - Two-handled interactive range slider to trim start and end points directly in the built-in video player.
  - Keyframe-accurate lossless stream-copy trimming via native FFmpeg backend without re-encoding.
  - Dedicated "Trim" button with progressive timecode readout (`00:00 / 00:00`), live slider feedback, auto-pausing playback on thumb drag to eliminate jitter, and automatic thumbnail update after trimming.
- **Unsaved Settings Confirmation Dialog**:
  - Built-in detection of pending configuration changes (`HasUnsavedSettings`).
  - Safe confirmation prompt (*"You have unsaved changes in settings. Would you like to save them before leaving?"* / *"У вас есть несохранённые изменения в настройках. Сохранить их перед переходом?"*) with `[Yes]` / `[No]` / `[Cancel]` actions when switching tabs within Settings, navigating away to other pages (Dashboard, Gallery, Diagnostics), or closing/minimizing the window.
  - Selecting "Yes" validates and applies settings cleanly; "No" discards modifications; "Cancel" aborts navigation and remains on the current view.
- **Light & Dark Theme Switcher & Full Bilingual Localization**:
  - Instant one-click theme switcher (`🌙 DARK` / `☀️ LIGHT`) with live palette swap across all UI controls.
  - Complete Russian and English language support across all dialogs, controls, navigation, and system notifications.

### Fixed
- **Monitor Capture Alt-Tab & Minimize Robustness**:
  - Fixed an issue where minimizing the game window (Alt-Tab) interrupted the recording buffer when "Selected Monitor" capture was active. Minimized window states (`IsIconic`) and active game process lifetimes (`HasGameProcess`) are now accurately tracked.
- **Settings Switch Buffer Continuation**:
  - Resolved buffer restart race condition when switching capture source from Game Window to Monitor during an active match.
- **Gallery Clip Reload on Navigation**:
  - Fixed clip viewer state retention when switching between views during video playback.

---

## [0.1.5] - 2026-10-10

### Added
- **Full Bilingual Localization (Russian & English)**:
  - Instant one-click language toggle button (`RU / EN` / `EN / RU`) in the header bar.
  - Complete translations across all views: Dashboard, Clip Gallery, Settings, Diagnostics, Setup Wizard, and System Tray menu.
  - Persistent language preference saved in `config.json`.
- **Light & Dark Theme Switcher**:
  - One-click theme toggle button (`🌙 DARK` / `☀️ LIGHT`) with live theme switching without app restart.
  - Full modern Light palette matching studio aesthetic (`#F2F5F3` background, `#FFFFFF` cards, `#3C662E` accents).
  - Clean video screen background in empty player state with localized hint icons.
  - Persistent theme preference saved in `config.json`.
- **Automatic GitHub Update Checker**:
  - Built-in GitHub Releases update check with header badge notifications (`UPDATE AVAILABLE ↗`).
  - Manual "Check for updates" button in Settings with localized status feedback.
- **Adaptive Gallery Grid**:
  - Replaced fixed-width wrap panel with an adaptive `UniformGrid`.
  - Automatically calculates column count and expands tile widths to symmetrically fill available window width across any screen resolution and window size.

### Fixed
- **Settings ComboBox Localization Bug**: Fixed an issue where changing languages would clear combobox selections (Monitor, Audio Output, Microphone, Resolution, Encoder, Codec). Selections now smoothly rebind and preserve saved IDs across language switches.
- **Dynamic Theme Resourcing**: Converted all static resource bindings across views to dynamic resources, ensuring complete, artifact-free theme swaps in both directions (Dark ➔ Light and Light ➔ Dark).
- **Audio Slider Mouse Wheel Sensitivity**: Volume slider scrolling now uses smooth 5% increments with localized tooltip indicators.

---

## [0.1.4] - 2026-10-10

### Added
- **In-process Native Video Player**:
  - Embedded FFmpeg video playback engine with smooth seeking, Play/Pause toggle, and direct frame rendering via `WriteableBitmap`.
- **Hover Thumbnail Scrubbing**:
  - Floating preview thumbnail card tracking seek bar mouse hover.
- **Volume & Mute Controls**:
  - Volume slider and one-click mute/unmute with mouse wheel support.
- **Clip Management**:
  - Rename clip with safe title sanitization, delete clip with confirmation, and open in external system player.
- **NVIDIA Container Auto-Mitigation**:
  - Automated detection and graceful pausing/restoring of `NvContainerLocalSystem` service during runtime to prevent IPC conflicts.

---

## [0.1.3] - 2026-10-10

### Initial Release
- Standalone portable native recorder for Hunt: Showdown 1896.
- Pure Windows Graphics Capture (WGC) + DirectX 11 capture pipeline.
- Circular RAM ring buffer with keyframe-accurate lossless MP4 export.
- Hardware encoding via NVIDIA NVENC, AMD AMF, Intel QSV, and CPU x264.
- Official signed NVIDIA MessageBus IPC integration safe for Easy Anti-Cheat.

```

`README.md`:

```md
# HuntReplay Studio

![HuntReplay Studio Overview](docs/screenshot.png)

[English](#english) | [Русский](#русский)

---

<a name="english"></a>
## English

**HuntReplay Studio** is a standalone, lightweight, zero-impact clip recorder designed specifically for **Hunt: Showdown 1896**. 

It automatically captures highlights (kills, deaths, downs) directly from the game's official Highlights SDK events, using hardware GPU encoding and Windows Graphics Capture (WGC). Works seamlessly on **AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs**.

### ✨ Features
- **Zero Injections & Anti-Cheat Safe**: Connects only through the standard NVIDIA MessageBus IPC pipe (`\\.\pipe\NvMessageBusBroadcast`). Uses an authentic signed `MessageBus.dll`. Zero keypress emulation, zero DLL hooking into the game process.
- **Hardware GPU Encoding**: Supports **NVIDIA NVENC**, **AMD AMF**, **Intel QSV**, and CPU (x264). Up to 120 FPS at 1080p, 1440p, or 4K.
- **Lossless Smart Trim**: Saves clips directly from a circular RAM ring buffer with keyframe-accurate trimming. No video re-encoding upon save.
- **Multi-Kill Coalescing**: Automatically stitches consecutive kills into a single action-packed highlight.
- **Standalone Portable EXE**: Single `.exe` binary with everything built-in. No Python, OBS, FFmpeg installations, or runtime dependencies required.
- **Dark Theme Gallery & Built-in Player**: Built-in 16:9/16:10 video player with sleek playback controls, instant search, renaming, and folder reveal.
- **NVIDIA Safety Safeguards**: Automatically detects if the official NVIDIA Container (`nvcontainer.exe`) is running and pauses its own IPC server to avoid conflicts.

### 🚀 Getting Started

1. Download the latest `HuntReplayStudio.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/Mlovo/HuntOpenHighlights/releases).
2. Run `HuntReplayStudio.exe`.
3. Complete the quick initial setup wizard (confirms NVIDIA MessageBus registration).
4. Play! Clips will be saved automatically upon kills and downs into your configured library directory.

> **Note for NVIDIA Users:**  
> If you have GeForce Experience or NVIDIA App installed, disable auto-highlights in their overlay settings (*Settings ➔ Highlights ➔ Off*) so they don't conflict with HuntReplay Studio.

### 🛠 Building from Source
**Requirements:** Windows 10/11 x64, .NET 8 SDK, CMake 3.25+, Visual Studio 2022 / Build Tools (C++ workload).

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\Build.ps1
```
The output portable executable will be placed in `artifacts\publish\HuntReplayStudio.exe`.

---

<a name="русский"></a>
## Русский

**HuntReplay Studio** — легковесный автономный рекордер хайлайтов, созданный специально для **Hunt: Showdown 1896**.

Автоматически сохраняет моменты убийств и смертей через официальный протокол событий игры, используя аппаратное кодирование на видеокарте и Windows Graphics Capture (WGC). Работает на видеокартах **AMD, Intel и NVIDIA**.

### ✨ Возможности
- **Безопасно для античита (EAC)**: Подключение происходит исключительно через официальный протокол NVIDIA MessageBus (`\\.\pipe\NvMessageBusBroadcast`). Используется оригинальная библиотека с официальной цифровой подписью NVIDIA. Без инжектов в процесс игры и без эмуляции нажатий клавиш.
- **Аппаратное GPU-кодирование**: Поддержка **AMD AMF**, **NVIDIA NVENC**, **Intel QSV** и программного x264. Запись до 120 FPS в разрешениях 1080p, 1440p и 4K.
- **Lossless Smart Trim**: Клипы сохраняются из циклического буфера в оперативной памяти с точной привязкой к ключевым кадрам без повторного перекодирования.
- **Объединение серий убийств**: Несколько убийств подряд автоматически склеиваются в один непрерывный динамичный хайлайт.
- **Один портативный EXE-файл**: Никаких сторонних программ, Python, OBS или кодеков устанавливать не нужно — всё встроено в один файл.
- **Встроенная галерея и видеоплеер**: Удобный плеер с перемоткой, поиском по клипам, переименованием и открытием папки с файлами.
- **Защита от конфликтов с NVIDIA**: Программа автоматически проверяет статус официальной службы NVIDIA (`nvcontainer.exe`) и предотвращает конфликты с GeForce Experience / NVIDIA App.

### 🚀 Быстрый старт

1. Скачайте свежий `HuntReplayStudio.exe` из раздела [Releases](https://github.com/Mlovo/HuntOpenHighlights/releases).
2. Запустите `HuntReplayStudio.exe`.
3. Пройдите мастер первоначальной настройки (подтвердит регистрацию MessageBus).
4. Играйте! Клипы будут сохраняться автоматически в настроенную папку библиотеки.

> **Примечание для владельцев видеокарт NVIDIA:**  
> Если у вас установлен GeForce Experience или NVIDIA App, отключите автоматическую запись хайлайтов в оверлее (*Настройки ➔ Highlights ➔ Выключить*), чтобы они не спорили за события игры.

### 🛠 Сборка из исходников
**Требования:** Windows 10/11 x64, .NET 8 SDK, CMake 3.25+, Visual Studio 2022 (компоненты C++).

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\Build.ps1
```
Готовый исполняемый файл появится в `artifacts\publish\HuntReplayStudio.exe`.

`TEST_INFRA.md`:

```md
# HuntReplayStudio Interactive Video Trimming — E2E Test Infrastructure (Tiers 1-4)

## 1. Overview & Architecture
This document defines the comprehensive opaque-box, requirement-driven End-to-End (E2E) testing infrastructure for the **HuntReplayStudio Interactive Video Trimming** system.

The E2E test suite validates the trimming feature across both managed WPF/MVVM layers (`GalleryView`, `RangeSlider`, `VideoTrimmingService`) and the native multimedia engine (`HuntReplay.Media.dll` wrapping FFmpeg 8.1.3). Test IDs cite three requirement groups: **§R1** the trim UI in the gallery player, **§R2** the trimming engine and service, **§R3** clips without audio and the unchanged normal player. `tools/Build.ps1` runs the suite after the Windows tests.

### Key Architectural Principles
- **Opaque-Box & Requirement-Driven**: Tests interact exclusively through public APIs, user interface state contracts, and exported C ABI functions, verifying external observable behaviors without relying on white-box internals.
- **Deterministic Synthetic Fixtures**: Sample video and multi-track audio clips are synthesized dynamically using bundled FFmpeg (`testsrc`, `sine`) with fixed GOP sizes and known audio frequencies. Tests do not depend on external downloads or game installations.
- **Strict Non-Destructive Invariants**: Verifies before and after every operation that source video files are untouched (via SHA-256 and modification timestamps).
- **Packet-Level Ground Truth**: Validates stream integrity, multi-track audio preservation, DTS monotonicity, and Audio/Video synchronization drift (< 25ms) via bundled `ffprobe`.

---

## 2. Test Suite Structure & Tier Breakdown

The test suite is structured across 4 distinct verification tiers totaling 39 automated end-to-end tests:

```
tests/HuntReplay.E2ETests/
├── HuntReplay.E2ETests.csproj       # .NET 8 Windows WPF test harness project
├── E2EInfrastructure.cs             # Shared test harness, FFmpeg/ffprobe wrappers, assertions, native loader
├── Tier1_FeatureCoverageTests.cs    # Tier 1: Isolated requirement happy paths (15 tests)
├── Tier2_BoundaryTests.cs           # Tier 2: Boundary conditions & corner cases (13 tests)
├── Tier3_CrossFeatureTests.cs       # Tier 3: Cross-feature combinations & pairwise workflows (6 tests)
├── Tier4_RealWorldScenariosTests.cs # Tier 4: Real-world gameplay highlight scenarios (5 tests)
└── Program.cs                       # MSTest entry: registers the four tiers as test cases on one STA thread
```

### Tier 1: Feature Coverage (Isolated Happy Path) — 15 Tests
Verifies happy-path execution of each isolated requirement:
- **T1-01 (§R1)**: "Trim Video" button presence and smooth inline mode entry in `GalleryView` (Seek slider swapped for `RangeSlider` and `TrimToolbar`, player paused).
- **T1-02 (§R1)**: Dual-handle timeline initialization to clip duration, visual distinction (accent selected range, dimmed unselected regions).
- **T1-03 (§R1)**: Real-time timestamp formatting in MM:SS (sub-hour) and HH:MM:SS (hour-plus) updating dynamically.
- **T1-04 (§R1)**: Fine-tuning stepping buttons (-0.1s / +0.1s) for start and end boundaries with precise clamping.
- **T1-05 (§R1)**: Mark In `[I]` and Mark Out `[O]` setting boundaries to current player PTS.
- **T1-06 (§R1)**: Selection preview playback starting at `SelectionStart` and automatically halting at `SelectionEnd`.
- **T1-07 (§R1)**: "Cancel" ("Отмена") action cleanly restoring normal player state with zero side effects or file alterations.
- **T1-08 (§R2)**: Native fast stream copying (`accurate=0`) remuxing packets without re-encoding, preserving H.264 video & AAC audio.
- **T1-09 (§R2)**: Native frame-accurate trimming mode flag (`accurate=1`) executing successfully.
- **T1-10 (§R2)**: Multi-track audio preservation retaining all audio tracks with original sample rates and channel layouts.
- **T1-11 (§R2)**: Audio/Video synchronization packet timestamps maintaining strict drift < 25ms.
- **T1-12 (§R2)**: Source video file immutability across multiple trimming operations.
- **T1-13 (§R2)**: Asynchronous trimming service progress reporting reaching 1.0 (100%).
- **T1-14 (§R3)**: Audio-less video trimming preserving video stream cleanly without missing audio crashes.
- **T1-15 (§R3)**: Standard player non-regression outside trim mode (normal playback, volume slider, mute toggle).

### Tier 2: Boundary & Corner Cases — 13 Tests
Stress-tests domain boundaries, invalid parameters, and extreme conditions:
- **T2-01 (§R1, §R2)**: Sub-0.5s minimum duration constraint enforced by both UI and service layers.
- **T2-02 (§R1)**: Crossing boundaries prevented (Start pushed past End clamps to `End - 0.5s`; End pushed before Start clamps to `Start + 0.5s`).
- **T2-03 (§R2)**: Trimming from origin `t = 0.0s` produces valid stream starting at PTS 0.000s.
- **T2-04 (§R2)**: Trimming up to exact clip duration handles EOF cleanly without overrun.
- **T2-05 (§R2)**: Narrow slice near end of long recording [58.0s, 59.5s] remuxes accurately.
- **T2-06 (§R1, §R2)**: Out-of-bounds, negative, NaN, and Infinity timestamps rejected safely.
- **T2-07 (§R2)**: Identical source and target paths rejected (including case-insensitive Windows match) to prevent overwriting source.
- **T2-08 (§R2)**: Missing, empty, or whitespace source paths fail validation with clear exceptions.
- **T2-09 (§R2)**: Cancellation mid-flight aborts promptly (< 250ms) and cleans up partial target files across 0%, 50%, and 95% progress points.
- **T2-10 (§R2)**: 3-track multi-audio preservation (48kHz stereo, 44.1kHz mono, 32kHz stereo) retains all distinct attributes.
- **T2-11 (§R2)**: Long recording 60s trimming maintains strictly monotonic packet DTS.
- **T2-12 (§R1)**: Translation dragging of range bar preserves duration window invariant.
- **T2-13 (§R1)**: Reducing Maximum below current RangeEnd safely coerces bounds without violating `RangeStart <= RangeEnd <= Maximum`.

### Tier 3: Cross-Feature Combinations & Pairwise Interactions — 6 Tests
Verifies interactions between disparate features:
- **T3-01 (§R1)**: Interactive workflow: fine-tune stepping -> jump to start -> preview playback -> automatic pause at boundary.
- **T3-02 (§R1, §R2)**: Mark In `[I]` & Mark Out `[O]` followed by direct export and boundary duration verification.
- **T3-03 (§R1, §R2)**: Export cancellation cleans up resources and allows clean trim mode exit restoring normal player.
- **T3-04 (§R2)**: Consecutive trimming passes on the same source video remain independent and preserve source integrity.
- **T3-05 (§R2)**: Concurrent multi-threaded trimming across 8 threads isolates thread-local state and error reporting (`hr_last_error`).
- **T3-06 (§R1)**: LiveSeek scrubbing event updates playhead and player frame smoothly.

### Tier 4: Real-World Application Scenarios — 5 Tests
Validates complete user workflows matching real game replay usage:
- **T4-01 (§R1, §R2)**: Realistic game replay 30s recording trimmed to 7s highlight and playable in native player engine with thumbnail extraction.
- **T4-02 (§R2)**: Gameplay clip with multi-track commentary (game sound + mic) preserves A/V sync (< 25ms drift).
- **T4-03 (§R2, §R3)**: Silent gameplay clip highlight extraction and thumbnail verification.
- **T4-04 (§R1, §R2)**: Multi-highlight batch extraction from match recording registered in `ClipLibrary` with metadata sidecars.
- **T4-05 (§R2, §R3)**: Long gameplay recording (60s) final clutch play extraction near EOF with clean native playback.

---

## 3. Test Runner & Execution Methods

All three suites (`HuntReplay.Tests`, `HuntReplay.WindowsTests`, `HuntReplay.E2ETests`) are MSTest projects on
Microsoft.Testing.Platform. Each project is a self-running test executable; every `Test("name", ...)` in the suites is
reported as its own test case. The WPF suites run on one shared STA thread (`tests/Shared/StaWorker.cs`).

### Method 1: .NET CLI Direct Execution
```powershell
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.E2ETests
```
Expected output: `total: 39, failed: 0, succeeded: 39`, exit code 0.

Run a subset by test name (each E2E case name starts with its tier):
```powershell
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.E2ETests -- --filter "Name~Tier 2"
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.Tests -- --filter "Name~trim"
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.Tests -- --list-tests
```

### Method 2: Full Solution Build & Verification
```powershell
dotnet build HuntReplayStudio.sln
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.Tests
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.WindowsTests
dotnet run --project tests/HuntReplay.E2ETests
```

### Manual: live IPC smoke check against a running Studio
```powershell
dotnet run --project tools/PipeSmoke -- --multi
```

---

## 4. Test Verification Invariants & Tolerances
| Invariant | Authoritative Requirement | Tolerance / Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Non-destructive source | §R2 Never overwrite source file | Byte-for-byte SHA256 identical, LastWriteTime untouched |
| Audio/Video sync drift | §R2 Maintain A/V synchronization | Offset difference between target & source < 25.0 ms |
| Minimum clip duration | §R1 Start strictly precedes end | Duration >= 0.5 s; sub-0.5s clamped or rejected |
| Multi-track audio | §R2 Accurately preserve audio tracks | All audio tracks preserved with original sample rate & channels |
| DTS monotonicity | §R2 Packet remuxing | Target packet DTS strictly monotonically increasing |
| Prompt cancellation | §R2 Support user cancellation | Abort in < 250 ms, target file deleted from disk |
| Native error reporting | §R2 Robust error handling | Negative return code and non-empty `hr_last_error()` |

```

# Third-party components / redistribution checklist

## HuntOpenHighlights source

The protocol and highlight scheduling logic originate from the HuntOpenHighlights baseline.
The application is a complete native/WPF rewrite and does not use Python or OBS.
This repository's own source is offered under MIT; see `LICENSE`.

## NVIDIA MessageBus.dll — proprietary, NOT MIT / NOT GPL

- Supplied by the original repository at `bin/MessageBus.dll`; not modified.
- SHA-256: `64e300997b5796da22ad8baa49e4eb919cdc170157cbe6770279f94508a84650`.
- The installer verifies that exact hash, `WinVerifyTrust` and the NVIDIA
  Corporation signer on the target Windows system. No counterfeit signature,
  replacement GfeSDK DLL, or game-file patch is created.
- A valid Authenticode signature proves origin/integrity, **not permission to
  redistribute, SDK authorization, NVIDIA endorsement or anti-cheat approval**.
- This repository does not grant NVIDIA redistribution rights. Confirm the
  applicable NVIDIA license before publishing an installer that embeds this file.
  If those rights cannot be established, do not publish that binary distribution.

## FFmpeg and bundled codec implementations

The default build uses the **GPL shared** BtbN FFmpeg SDK because the requested
explicit CPU fallback is `libx264`. AMF, NVENC and QSV remain driver-dependent.

Exact binary URL, SHA-256, upstream revision and build-recipe revision are in
`tools/ffmpeg.lock.json`. There is no `latest` resolution or download at app runtime.
The package's DLLs are embedded; **ffmpeg.exe / ffprobe.exe are not used or bundled
as the recording backend**.

Relevant source locations:

- https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/tree/330caae0c1acccd2222edc52a05940c574561ce5
- https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/tree/9acad4a9ef1583096af7836cc1e9c8cbcb4d3950

`licenses/FFmpeg-GPLv3.txt` contains upstream's GPLv3 text. Review the actual
archive's configuration and third-party notices: optional codec libraries have
their own licenses. The default combined, linked application distribution must
comply with GPLv3-compatible obligations; the MIT grant for our source does not
remove those obligations. Distributors must supply complete corresponding source
(including enabled dependency sources, modifications and build instructions) by
a GPL-compliant method. Merely including these two links or an unfulfilled source
offer is **not** a substitute. Preserve the exact source bundle/build manifest
alongside any public release. Hosted CI artifacts are unsigned QA builds, not a
statement that distribution rights or license compliance have been cleared.

An LGPL-only build can be engineered separately, but it will not contain x264;
remove/disable that setting rather than claiming the encoder exists. Do not swap
arbitrary DLL versions into the pinned runtime without rebuilding and retesting.

## .NET / WPF / Windows SDK

.NET 8 and WPF are Microsoft/.NET Foundation projects, primarily MIT. The
self-contained runtime is supplied by the .NET SDK during publishing. Preserve
its third-party license notices when redistributing:

- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime
- https://github.com/dotnet/wpf

Windows OS APIs and installed GPU drivers are system prerequisites, not supplied
by this project. NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Hunt: Showdown and Windows are trademarks of
their respective owners. No endorsement or certification is claimed.

## Managed dependencies

- Google.Protobuf 3.36.2 — BSD-3-Clause; `licenses/Google.Protobuf.txt`.
- Grpc.Tools 2.84.0 — Apache-2.0 build tools, not an end-user dependency.
- Microsoft.Toolkit.Uwp.Notifications 7.1.3 — MIT, used for native Windows toasts.

These are fixed package versions in the project files. Preserve upstream notices
for all resolved/transitive dependencies in a shipped source/binary bundle.

## Signing releases

MessageBus.dll's signature must remain unchanged. This repository contains no
code-signing private key and does not manufacture a publisher identity. Sign your
own final `.exe` with a legitimate Authenticode code-signing certificate, verify
it after signing, and regenerate release checksums. If signing the native engine
as well, do so **before** creating the embedded runtime hash manifest. The
unsigned development build may trigger SmartScreen / show an unknown publisher.

`native/CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(HuntReplayMedia VERSION 0.1.1 LANGUAGES CXX)
if(NOT WIN32 OR NOT MSVC OR NOT CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P EQUAL 8)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "Build with Visual Studio 2022 x64 and Windows SDK 10.0.22621+ on Windows.")
endif()
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>")
set(FFMPEG_ROOT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/vendor/ffmpeg" CACHE PATH "Pinned FFmpeg shared SDK")
find_path(FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR libavcodec/avcodec.h PATHS "${FFMPEG_ROOT}/include" NO_DEFAULT_PATH REQUIRED)
add_library(HuntReplay.Media SHARED src/api.cpp src/capture.cpp src/video.cpp src/audio.cpp src/devices.cpp src/mux.cpp src/player.cpp src/trim.cpp)
target_include_directories(HuntReplay.Media PRIVATE include "${FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR}")
target_compile_definitions(HuntReplay.Media PRIVATE UNICODE _UNICODE _WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 WINVER=0x0A00)
target_compile_options(HuntReplay.Media PRIVATE /W4 /EHsc /permissive- /utf-8 /Zc:__cplusplus)
target_link_libraries(HuntReplay.Media PRIVATE d3d11 dxgi dxguid windowsapp runtimeobject ole32 uuid propsys avrt)
foreach(component avcodec avformat avutil swresample swscale)
  find_library(FFMPEG_${component} NAMES ${component} PATHS "${FFMPEG_ROOT}/lib" NO_DEFAULT_PATH REQUIRED)
  target_link_libraries(HuntReplay.Media PRIVATE "${FFMPEG_${component}}")
endforeach()
set_target_properties(HuntReplay.Media PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME "HuntReplay.Media")
install(TARGETS HuntReplay.Media RUNTIME DESTINATION .)

```

`native/include/huntreplay_media.h`:

```h
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#define HR_API extern "C" __declspec(dllexport)
#define HR_CALL __cdecl
#else
#error HuntReplay.Media requires Windows 10 2004 or newer, x64.
#endif

// Versioned C ABI. No C++ objects, ownership or exceptions cross this boundary.
struct hr_config {
    uint32_t size;
    int32_t encoder; // 0 auto, 1 AMF, 2 NVENC, 3 QSV, 4 x264 (explicit only)
    int32_t codec;   // 0 H264, 1 HEVC, 2 AV1
    int32_t fps, width, height, bitrate, gop_seconds;
    uint64_t window, monitor;
    const wchar_t* output_device;
    const wchar_t* microphone_device;
    int32_t microphone_enabled;
    float microphone_gain;
    int32_t separate_microphone;
    const wchar_t* gpu_device;
};
struct hr_packet {
    int32_t stream, keyframe;
    int64_t pts_us, dts_us, duration_us;
    const uint8_t* data;
    int32_t size;
};
struct hr_stats {
    int64_t frames, dropped_frames, encoded_bytes, elapsed_us;
    int32_t width, height, encoder, codec, running, source_stale;
};
struct hr_device {
    int32_t kind, is_default, vendor; // kind: 0 monitor, 1 render endpoint, 2 microphone, 3 GPU
    uint64_t handle;
    const wchar_t* id;
    const wchar_t* name;
};
struct hr_session;
struct hr_mux;
struct hr_player;
typedef void (HR_CALL *hr_packet_callback)(void* user, const hr_packet* packet);
typedef void (HR_CALL *hr_log_callback)(void* user, int32_t level, const char* utf8_message);
typedef void (HR_CALL *hr_device_callback)(void* user, const hr_device* device);
typedef int (HR_CALL *hr_trim_progress_callback)(void* user, double progress);

HR_API int HR_CALL hr_abi_version();
HR_API const wchar_t* HR_CALL hr_last_error(); // Thread-local, valid until next failing API call.
HR_API int HR_CALL hr_devices(hr_device_callback callback, void* user);
HR_API int HR_CALL hr_probe(const hr_config* config); // Synthetic GPU frames + 200ms WASAPI/AAC probe; no file is written.
HR_API int HR_CALL hr_start(const hr_config* config, hr_packet_callback packets, hr_log_callback logs,
                           void* user, hr_session** result);
HR_API void HR_CALL hr_stop(hr_session* session); // Joins workers; preserves codec headers for export.

#include "common.h"

namespace hr {

thread_local std::wstring last_error;
template<typename F> int guard(F operation) noexcept {
    // Only FFmpeg warnings logged during this call may annotate its error, not one left over from an earlier call.
    ffmpeg_detail.clear();
    try { operation(); last_error.clear(); return 0; }
    catch (const winrt::hresult_error& e) { last_error = std::wstring(e.message()); }
    catch (const std::exception& e) { last_error = wide(e.what()); }
    catch (...) { last_error = L"Unknown native multimedia error"; }
    return -1;
}
}
int HR_CALL hr_abi_version() {
    static std::once_flag initialized;
    std::call_once(initialized, [] {
        av_log_set_callback([](void*, int level, const char* format, va_list arguments) {
            if (level > AV_LOG_WARNING) return;
            try {
                char buffer[2048]{};
                vsnprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer), format, arguments);
                hr::ffmpeg_detail = buffer;
            } catch (...) { }
        });
    });
    return 1;
}
const wchar_t* HR_CALL hr_last_error() { return hr::last_error.c_str(); }
int HR_CALL hr_devices(hr_device_callback callback, void* user) {
    return hr::guard([&] { if (!callback) throw std::runtime_error("Missing device callback."); hr::enumerate(callback, user); });
}
int HR_CALL hr_probe(const hr_config* source) {
    return hr::guard([&] {
        if (!source) throw std::runtime_error("Missing probe config.");
        auto config = *source; hr::validate(config);
        hr::Apartment apartment;
        auto window = reinterpret_cast<HWND>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(config.window));
        auto monitor = window ? MonitorFromWindow(window, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST)
            : reinterpret_cast<HMONITOR>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(config.monitor));
        if (!monitor) monitor = MonitorFromPoint(POINT{0, 0}, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY);
        hr::D3D d3d(monitor, config.gpu_device);
        if (!config.width || !config.height) {
            RECT area{};
            if (window) hr::check(GetClientRect(window, &area) ? S_OK : HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()));
            else {
                MONITORINFO info{}; info.cbSize = sizeof(info);
                hr::check(GetMonitorInfoW(monitor, &info) ? S_OK : HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()));
                area = info.rcMonitor;
            }
            if (area.right - area.left < 2 || area.bottom - area.top < 2) throw std::runtime_error("Probe target has no usable dimensions.");
            hr::fit_output(config, area.right - area.left, area.bottom - area.top);
            hr::validate(config);
        }
        int encoded = 0;
        hr::VideoEncoder encoder(d3d, config, [&](int, const AVPacket*, AVRational) { ++encoded; });
        D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC desc{};
        desc.Width = config.width; desc.Height = config.height; desc.MipLevels = 1; desc.ArraySize = 1;
        desc.Format = DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM; desc.SampleDesc.Count = 1; desc.BindFlags = D3D11_BIND_RENDER_TARGET;
        hr::ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> black; hr::check(d3d.device->CreateTexture2D(&desc, nullptr, &black));
        hr::ComPtr<ID3D11RenderTargetView> view; hr::check(d3d.device->CreateRenderTargetView(black.Get(), nullptr, &view));
        const float color[]{0, 0, 0, 1}; d3d.context->ClearRenderTargetView(view.Get(), color);
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) encoder.encode(black.Get(), config.width, config.height, i);
        encoder.drain(true);
        if (encoded == 0) throw std::runtime_error("Encoder accepted input but produced no packets.");
        int audio_packets = 0;
        std::string audio_failure;
        hr::AudioCapture audio(config, hr::qpc_100ns(),
            [&](int, const AVPacket*, AVRational) { ++audio_packets; },
            [&](std::string message) { audio_failure = std::move(message); });
        audio.start();
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(200));
        audio.stop(); // Join before reading the callback-owned probe results.
        if (!audio_failure.empty()) throw std::runtime_error(audio_failure);
        if (audio_packets == 0) throw std::runtime_error("WASAPI/AAC probe produced no packets.");
    });
}
int HR_CALL hr_start(const hr_config* config, hr_packet_callback packets, hr_log_callback logs, void* user, hr_session** result) {
    if (result) *result = nullptr;

        auto session = std::make_unique<hr_session>(*config, packets, logs, user);
        session->start(); *result = session.release();
    });
}

`native/src/audio.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common.h"
#include <ksmedia.h>
#include <avrt.h>

namespace hr {
namespace {
constexpr int rate = 48000;
constexpr int timeline_size = rate * 4;

// Sparse timestamped PCM ring. Silence is synthesized on the same QPC timeline when WASAPI
// emits no packets (e.g. a silent desktop); this prevents AAC from drifting behind video.
struct Timeline {
    std::vector<float> samples = std::vector<float>(timeline_size * 2);
    std::vector<int64_t> stamps = std::vector<int64_t>(timeline_size, INT64_MIN);
    void write(int64_t at, const float* data, int count) {
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            int64_t tick = at + i;
            if (tick < 0) continue;
            auto index = static_cast<size_t>(tick % timeline_size);
            samples[index * 2] = data[i * 2]; samples[index * 2 + 1] = data[i * 2 + 1]; stamps[index] = tick;
        }
    }
    float get(int64_t at, int channel) const {
        if (at < 0) return 0;
        auto index = static_cast<size_t>(at % timeline_size);
        return stamps[index] == at ? samples[index * 2 + channel] : 0;
    }
};
struct WaveDelete { void operator()(WAVEFORMATEX* p) const { CoTaskMemFree(p); } };
struct SwrDelete { void operator()(SwrContext* p) const { swr_free(&p); } };
struct Endpoint {
    ComPtr<IAudioClient> client;
    ComPtr<IAudioCaptureClient> capture;
    std::unique_ptr<WAVEFORMATEX, WaveDelete> format;
    std::unique_ptr<SwrContext, SwrDelete> resampler;
    Handle event{CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr)};
    Timeline timeline;
    bool packed24 = false;
    int64_t next_sample = -1;
    int64_t epoch;
    uint64_t expected_position = 0;
    std::wstring device_id;
    // Reused by read() on every WASAPI packet (~10 ms) to keep the audio thread allocation-free in steady state.
    std::vector<uint8_t> silence;
    std::vector<float> unpacked, converted;

    Endpoint(IMMDeviceEnumerator* enumerator, const wchar_t* id, bool loopback, int64_t epoch_100ns) : epoch(epoch_100ns) {
        ComPtr<IMMDevice> device;
        if (id && *id) check(enumerator->GetDevice(id, &device));
        else check(enumerator->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(loopback ? eRender : eCapture, eConsole, &device));
        LPWSTR endpoint_id = nullptr; check(device->GetId(&endpoint_id));
        device_id = endpoint_id; CoTaskMemFree(endpoint_id);
        check(device->Activate(__uuidof(IAudioClient), CLSCTX_ALL, nullptr, reinterpret_cast<void**>(client.GetAddressOf())));
        WAVEFORMATEX* raw = nullptr; check(client->GetMixFormat(&raw)); format.reset(raw);
        if (raw->nChannels < 1 || raw->nChannels > 32 || raw->nSamplesPerSec < 8000 ||
            raw->nSamplesPerSec > 384000 || raw->nBlockAlign == 0)
            throw std::runtime_error("Invalid WASAPI endpoint format.");
        AVSampleFormat sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_NONE;
        GUID subtype{};
        uint64_t mask = 0;
        if (raw->wFormatTag == WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE) {
            auto* ext = reinterpret_cast<WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE*>(raw);
            subtype = ext->SubFormat; mask = ext->dwChannelMask;
        } else if (raw->wFormatTag == WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT) subtype = KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_IEEE_FLOAT;
        else if (raw->wFormatTag == WAVE_FORMAT_PCM) subtype = KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_PCM;
        if (subtype == KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_IEEE_FLOAT && raw->wBitsPerSample == 32) sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_FLT;
        else if (subtype == KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_PCM) {
            switch (raw->wBitsPerSample) {
                case 8: sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_U8; break;
                case 16: sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_S16; break;
                case 24: packed24 = true; sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_FLT; break;
                case 32: sample_format = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_S32; break;
            }
        }
        if (sample_format == AV_SAMPLE_FMT_NONE) throw std::runtime_error("Unsupported WASAPI endpoint mix format.");
        AVChannelLayout input{}, output = AV_CHANNEL_LAYOUT_STEREO;
        if (mask) avcheck(av_channel_layout_from_mask(&input, mask), "Audio channel mask");
        else av_channel_layout_default(&input, raw->nChannels);
        SwrContext* swr = nullptr;
        int result = swr_alloc_set_opts2(&swr, &output, AV_SAMPLE_FMT_FLT, rate,
            &input, sample_format, raw->nSamplesPerSec, 0, nullptr);
        av_channel_layout_uninit(&input);
        resampler.reset(swr); avcheck(result, "Create audio resampler");
        avcheck(swr_init(resampler.get()), "Initialize audio resampler");
        DWORD flags = AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_EVENTCALLBACK | (loopback ? AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK : 0);
        check(client->Initialize(AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_SHARED, flags, 1'000'000, 0, raw, nullptr));
        if (!event.value) check(HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()));
        check(client->SetEventHandle(event.value));
        check(client->GetService(IID_PPV_ARGS(&capture)));
    }
    void read() {
        UINT32 available = 0; check(capture->GetNextPacketSize(&available));
        while (available) {
            BYTE* data = nullptr; UINT32 frames = 0; DWORD flags = 0;
            UINT64 position = 0, timestamp = 0;
            HRESULT status = capture->GetBuffer(&data, &frames, &flags, &position, &timestamp);
            if (status == AUDCLNT_S_BUFFER_EMPTY) break;
            check(status);
            try {
                int64_t at = (flags & AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_TIMESTAMP_ERROR)
                    ? av_rescale(qpc_100ns() - epoch, rate, 10'000'000) - frames * rate / format->nSamplesPerSec
                    : av_rescale(static_cast<int64_t>(timestamp) - epoch, rate, 10'000'000);
                if (next_sample < 0 || std::abs(at - next_sample) > rate / 10 ||
                    ((flags & AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_DATA_DISCONTINUITY) && position != expected_position)) {
                    swr_close(resampler.get()); avcheck(swr_init(resampler.get()), "Reset discontinuous audio");
                    next_sample = at;
                } else if (std::abs(at - next_sample) > rate / 1000) {
                    // Smooth independent device-clock drift rather than accumulating A/V error.
                    avcheck(swr_set_compensation(resampler.get(), static_cast<int>(at - next_sample), rate), "Audio clock compensation");
                }
                expected_position = position + frames;
                if (flags & AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT) {
                    silence.assign(static_cast<size_t>(frames) * format->nBlockAlign,
                        format->wBitsPerSample == 8 ? 128 : 0);
                    data = silence.data();
                }
                if (packed24) {
                    unpacked.resize(static_cast<size_t>(frames) * format->nChannels);
                    for (size_t i = 0; i < unpacked.size(); ++i) {
                        const uint8_t* p = data + i * 3;
                        int32_t value = (p[0] | (p[1] << 8) | (p[2] << 16));
                        if (value & 0x800000) value |= static_cast<int32_t>(0xff000000u);
                        unpacked[i] = value / 8388608.f;
                    }
                    data = reinterpret_cast<BYTE*>(unpacked.data());
                }
                int capacity = static_cast<int>(av_rescale_rnd(swr_get_delay(resampler.get(), format->nSamplesPerSec) + frames,
                    rate, format->nSamplesPerSec, AV_ROUND_UP)) + 256;
                converted.resize(static_cast<size_t>(capacity) * 2);
                uint8_t* target = reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(converted.data());
                const uint8_t* source = data;
                int count = swr_convert(resampler.get(), &target, capacity, &source, frames);
                avcheck(count, "Resample audio");
                timeline.write(next_sample, converted.data(), count);
                next_sample += count;
            } catch (...) { capture->ReleaseBuffer(frames); throw; }
            check(capture->ReleaseBuffer(frames));
            check(capture->GetNextPacketSize(&available));
        }
    }
};

Codec audio_encoder() {
    auto* implementation = avcodec_find_encoder(AV_CODEC_ID_AAC);
    if (!implementation) throw std::runtime_error("AAC encoder missing from native runtime.");
    Codec codec(avcodec_alloc_context3(implementation));
    if (!codec) throw std::bad_alloc();
    codec->sample_rate = rate; codec->sample_fmt = AV_SAMPLE_FMT_FLTP;
    codec->bit_rate = 192000; codec->time_base = AVRational{1, rate};
    av_channel_layout_default(&codec->ch_layout, 2);
    codec->flags |= AV_CODEC_FLAG_GLOBAL_HEADER;
    avcheck(avcodec_open2(codec.get(), implementation, nullptr), "Open AAC encoder");
    return codec;
}
}

struct AudioCapture::Impl {
    AudioCapture& owner;
    hr_config config;
    std::wstring output_id, microphone_id;
    int64_t epoch;
    Emit emit;
    std::function<void(std::string)> fail, note;
    std::jthread thread;
    std::promise<void> ready;
    explicit Impl(AudioCapture& parent, const hr_config& source, int64_t epoch_100ns, Emit emit,
                  std::function<void(std::string)> fail, std::function<void(std::string)> note)
        : owner(parent), config(source), epoch(epoch_100ns), emit(std::move(emit)), fail(std::move(fail)), note(std::move(note)) {
        output_id = source.output_device ? source.output_device : L"";
        microphone_id = source.microphone_device ? source.microphone_device : L"";
    }
    Packet drained = make_packet(); // Reused by drain() for every AAC frame of every track.
    void drain(int index, bool flush = false) {
        auto* codec = owner.codecs[index].get();
        if (flush) avcheck(avcodec_send_frame(codec, nullptr), "Flush audio encoder");
        for (;;) {
            int result = avcodec_receive_packet(codec, drained.get());
            if (result == AVERROR(EAGAIN) || result == AVERROR_EOF) break;
            avcheck(result, "Receive AAC packet");
            emit(index + 1, drained.get(), codec->time_base); av_packet_unref(drained.get());
        }
    }
    void run(std::stop_token stop) {
        bool signaled = false;
        try {
            Apartment apartment;
            DWORD task_index = 0;
            HANDLE priority = AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW(L"Audio", &task_index);
            struct PriorityGuard { HANDLE h; ~PriorityGuard() { if (h) AvRevertMmThreadCharacteristics(h); } } priority_guard{priority};
            ComPtr<IMMDeviceEnumerator> enumerator;
            check(CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&enumerator)));
            auto game = std::make_unique<Endpoint>(enumerator.Get(), output_id.c_str(), true, epoch);
            std::unique_ptr<Endpoint> mic;
            if (config.microphone_enabled) mic = std::make_unique<Endpoint>(enumerator.Get(), microphone_id.c_str(), false, epoch);
            check(game->client->Start());
            if (mic) check(mic->client->Start());
            ready.set_value(); signaled = true;
            int frame_samples = owner.codecs[0]->frame_size;
            int64_t cursor = 0;
            HANDLE events[]{game->event.value, mic ? mic->event.value : game->event.value};
            // Endpoints that follow the Windows default device are reopened in place when the default changes or the
            // device disappears. The PCM timeline only gets a short silent gap; encoding and video never stop.
            // An explicitly selected device that disappears still ends the session, since nothing can replace it.
            auto reopen = [&](std::unique_ptr<Endpoint>& endpoint, bool loopback, const char* what) {
                if (endpoint) endpoint->client->Stop(); // Best effort: an invalidated client may refuse.
                endpoint = std::make_unique<Endpoint>(enumerator.Get(), L"", loopback, epoch);
                check(endpoint->client->Start());
                events[0] = game->event.value;
                events[1] = mic ? mic->event.value : game->event.value;
                if (note) note(std::string(what) + " changed; recording continues on the new Windows default device.");
            };
            auto follow_default = [&](std::unique_ptr<Endpoint>& endpoint, EDataFlow flow, bool loopback, const char* what) {
                ComPtr<IMMDevice> current;
                check(enumerator->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(flow, eConsole, &current));
                LPWSTR id = nullptr; check(current->GetId(&id));
                bool changed = endpoint->device_id != id; CoTaskMemFree(id);
                if (changed) reopen(endpoint, loopback, what);
            };
            auto read = [&](std::unique_ptr<Endpoint>& endpoint, bool follows_default, bool loopback, const char* what) {
                try { endpoint->read(); }
                catch (const winrt::hresult_error& e) {
                    if (!follows_default || e.code() != AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED) throw;
                    reopen(endpoint, loopback, what);
                }
            };
            auto next_device_check = Clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(1);
            // One PCM frame per track, allocated once. av_frame_make_writable only copies if the encoder still holds it.
            std::vector<Frame> pcm;
            for (const auto& codec : owner.codecs) {
                auto& frame = pcm.emplace_back(make_frame());
                frame->nb_samples = frame_samples; frame->sample_rate = rate; frame->format = codec->sample_fmt;
                avcheck(av_channel_layout_copy(&frame->ch_layout, &codec->ch_layout), "Copy AAC channel layout");
                avcheck(av_frame_get_buffer(frame.get(), 0), "Allocate AAC samples");
            }
            auto encode_until = [&](int64_t limit) {
                while (cursor + frame_samples <= limit) {
                    for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(owner.codecs.size()); ++i) {
                        auto* frame = pcm[i].get(); auto* codec = owner.codecs[i].get();
                        avcheck(av_frame_make_writable(frame), "Reuse AAC frame");
                        frame->pts = cursor;
                        for (int s = 0; s < frame_samples; ++s) for (int channel = 0; channel < 2; ++channel) {
                            float g = game->timeline.get(cursor + s, channel);
                            float m = mic ? mic->timeline.get(cursor + s, channel) * config.microphone_gain : 0;
                            float value = config.separate_microphone ? (i == 0 ? g : m) : g + m;
                            reinterpret_cast<float*>(frame->data[channel])[s] = std::clamp(value, -1.f, 1.f);
                        }
                        int result = avcodec_send_frame(codec, frame);
                        if (result == AVERROR(EAGAIN)) { drain(i); result = avcodec_send_frame(codec, frame); }
                        avcheck(result, "Encode AAC"); drain(i);
                    }
                    cursor += frame_samples;
                }
            };
            while (!stop.stop_requested()) {
                DWORD wait = WaitForMultipleObjects(mic ? 2 : 1, events, FALSE, 10);
                if (wait == WAIT_FAILED) check(HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()));
                read(game, output_id.empty(), true, "Default audio output");
                if (mic) read(mic, microphone_id.empty(), false, "Default microphone");
                if (Clock::now() >= next_device_check) {
                    if (output_id.empty()) follow_default(game, eRender, true, "Default audio output");
                    if (mic && microphone_id.empty()) follow_default(mic, eCapture, false, "Default microphone");
                    next_device_check = Clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(1);
                }
                // A bounded 120ms jitter buffer on the shared video/WASAPI QPC timeline.
                encode_until(av_rescale(qpc_100ns() - epoch, rate, 10'000'000) - rate * 120 / 1000);
            }
            game->read(); if (mic) mic->read();
            encode_until(av_rescale(qpc_100ns() - epoch, rate, 10'000'000));
            game->client->Stop(); if (mic) mic->client->Stop();
            for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(owner.codecs.size()); ++i) drain(i, true);
        } catch (const winrt::hresult_error& e) {
            if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception());
            else fail("WASAPI: " + winrt::to_string(e.message()) + " (selected device disconnected; restart buffer)");
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception()); else fail(std::string("Audio: ") + e.what());
        } catch (...) {
            if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception()); else fail("Unknown audio error");
        }
    }
};
AudioCapture::AudioCapture(const hr_config& config, int64_t epoch, Emit emit, std::function<void(std::string)> fail,
                           std::function<void(std::string)> note)
    : impl(std::make_unique<Impl>(*this, config, epoch, std::move(emit), std::move(fail), std::move(note))) {
    codecs.push_back(audio_encoder());
    if (config.microphone_enabled && config.separate_microphone) codecs.push_back(audio_encoder());
}
AudioCapture::~AudioCapture() { stop(); }
void AudioCapture::start() {
    auto ready = impl->ready.get_future();
    impl->thread = std::jthread([this](std::stop_token stop) { impl->run(stop); });
    ready.get();
}
void AudioCapture::stop() {
    if (impl->thread.joinable()) { impl->thread.request_stop(); impl->thread.join(); }
}
}

#include "common.h"
#include <winrt/Windows.Foundation.Metadata.h>
#include <winrt/Windows.Security.Authorization.AppCapabilityAccess.h>

namespace hr {
void validate(const hr_config& c) {
    if (c.size != sizeof(hr_config)) throw std::runtime_error("Native ABI/config version mismatch.");
    if (c.encoder < 0 || c.encoder > 4 || c.codec < 0 || c.codec > 2 ||
        (c.fps != 30 && c.fps != 60 && c.fps != 120) || c.bitrate < 10'000'000 || c.bitrate > 80'000'000 ||
        c.width < 0 || c.height < 0 || c.width > 8192 || c.height > 8192 ||
        (c.gop_seconds != 1 && c.gop_seconds != 2) ||
        !std::isfinite(c.microphone_gain) || c.microphone_gain < 0 || c.microphone_gain > 1)
        throw std::runtime_error("Invalid capture configuration.");
    if (c.encoder == 4 && c.codec != 0) throw std::runtime_error("CPU x264 supports H.264 only.");
}
// A height without a width keeps the source's aspect ratio and never scales the source up; no height records the
// source as it is. An explicit width and height are used unchanged. HuntReplay.Core VideoResolutions.OutputSize mirrors this.
void fit_output(hr_config& c, int source_width, int source_height) {
    if (c.width > 0 && c.height > 0) return;
    if (c.height <= 0 || c.height >= source_height) {
        c.width = (source_width / 2) * 2; c.height = (source_height / 2) * 2;
        return;
    }
    const long width = std::lround(static_cast<double>(source_width) * c.height / source_height);
    c.width = std::max(2, static_cast<int>(width / 2) * 2); c.height = (c.height / 2) * 2;
}
Session::Session(const hr_config& source, hr_packet_callback packet_cb, hr_log_callback log_cb, void* context)
    : config(source), packets(packet_cb), logs(log_cb), user(context) {
    validate(source);
    output_id = source.output_device ? source.output_device : L"";
    microphone_id = source.microphone_device ? source.microphone_device : L"";
    gpu_id = source.gpu_device ? source.gpu_device : L"";
    config.output_device = output_id.c_str(); config.microphone_device = microphone_id.c_str();
    config.gpu_device = gpu_id.c_str();
}
Session::~Session() { stop(); }
void Session::log(int level, const std::string& message) const { if (logs) logs(user, level, message.c_str()); }
void Session::emit(int stream, const AVPacket* packet, AVRational base) {
    if (packet->pts == AV_NOPTS_VALUE || packet->dts == AV_NOPTS_VALUE)
        throw std::runtime_error("Encoder returned a packet without timestamps.");
    if (stream == 0 && !video_header_frozen) {
        // Some hardware backends publish global/sequence headers with their FIRST packet,
        // not at avcodec_open2. Freeze a deep copy before that packet reaches the RAM ring.
        std::lock_guard lock(headers_mutex);
        auto* raw = avcodec_parameters_alloc(); if (!raw) throw std::bad_alloc();
        std::unique_ptr<AVCodecParameters, ParametersDelete> header(raw);
        avcheck(avcodec_parameters_from_context(raw, video->codec.get()), "Freeze video codec parameters");
        size_t extra_size = 0;
        const uint8_t* extra = av_packet_get_side_data(packet, AV_PKT_DATA_NEW_EXTRADATA, &extra_size);
        auto extracted = make_packet();
        if (raw->extradata_size == 0 && !extra) {
            struct Filter { AVBSFContext* value = nullptr; ~Filter() { av_bsf_free(&value); } } filter;
            const AVBitStreamFilter* implementation = av_bsf_get_by_name("extract_extradata");
            if (!implementation) throw std::runtime_error("The runtime lacks extract_extradata.");
            avcheck(av_bsf_alloc(implementation, &filter.value), "Allocate sequence header parser");
            avcheck(avcodec_parameters_copy(filter.value->par_in, raw), "Configure sequence header parser");
            filter.value->time_base_in = base;
            avcheck(av_bsf_init(filter.value), "Initialize sequence header parser");
            auto copy = make_packet(); avcheck(av_packet_ref(copy.get(), packet), "Reference header packet");
            avcheck(av_bsf_send_packet(filter.value, copy.get()), "Parse sequence header");
            avcheck(av_bsf_receive_packet(filter.value, extracted.get()), "Read sequence header");
            extra = av_packet_get_side_data(extracted.get(), AV_PKT_DATA_NEW_EXTRADATA, &extra_size);
        }
        if (extra && extra_size > 0) {
            if (extra_size > 1024 * 1024) throw std::runtime_error("Invalid encoder sequence header size.");
            av_freep(&raw->extradata);
            raw->extradata = static_cast<uint8_t*>(av_mallocz(extra_size + AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE));
            if (!raw->extradata) throw std::bad_alloc();
            memcpy(raw->extradata, extra, extra_size); raw->extradata_size = static_cast<int>(extra_size);
        }
        if (raw->extradata_size == 0) throw std::runtime_error("Encoder supplied no decodable global/sequence header. Update the driver or choose another codec.");
        headers[0] = std::move(header);
        video_header_frozen = true;
    }
    hr_packet data{};
    data.stream = stream; data.keyframe = (packet->flags & AV_PKT_FLAG_KEY) != 0;
    data.pts_us = av_rescale_q(packet->pts, base, microseconds);
    data.dts_us = av_rescale_q(packet->dts, base, microseconds);
    data.duration_us = av_rescale_q(packet->duration, base, microseconds);
    data.data = packet->data; data.size = packet->size;
    bytes.fetch_add(packet->size, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (packets) packets(user, &data);
}
void Session::start() {
    std::promise<void> ready;
    auto result = ready.get_future();
    worker = std::jthread([this, promise = std::move(ready)](std::stop_token token) mutable { capture(token, std::move(promise)); });
    result.get();
}
void Session::stop() {
    if (worker.joinable()) { worker.request_stop(); worker.join(); }
    running = false;
}
namespace {
// The capture thread never waits longer than this for Windows to answer the consent request.
constexpr auto border_consent_timeout = std::chrono::seconds(3);

const char* access_name(winrt::Windows::Security::Authorization::AppCapabilityAccess::AppCapabilityAccessStatus status) {
    using Status = winrt::Windows::Security::Authorization::AppCapabilityAccess::AppCapabilityAccessStatus;
    switch (status) {
        case Status::Allowed: return "Allowed";
        case Status::DeniedByUser: return "DeniedByUser";
        case Status::DeniedBySystem: return "DeniedBySystem";
        case Status::NotDeclaredByApp: return "NotDeclaredByApp";
        case Status::UserPromptRequired: return "UserPromptRequired";
        default: return "unknown status";
    }
}

// The official, consent-based request for borderless capture. It sets IsBorderRequired(false) only when Windows
// answers Allowed. Every other outcome keeps the OS indicator. The function never throws and never bypasses the answer.
std::string request_borderless(winrt::Windows::Graphics::Capture::GraphicsCaptureSession session) {
    using Status = winrt::Windows::Security::Authorization::AppCapabilityAccess::AppCapabilityAccessStatus;
    const std::string retained = "OS capture indicator is retained: ";
    try {
        if (!winrt::Windows::Foundation::Metadata::ApiInformation::IsPropertyPresent(
                L"Windows.Graphics.Capture.GraphicsCaptureSession", L"IsBorderRequired"))
            return retained + "this Windows build has no GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired.";
        auto answer = std::make_shared<std::promise<Status>>();
        auto pending = answer->get_future();
        std::thread([answer] {
            try {
                Apartment apartment;
                answer->set_value(winrt::Windows::Graphics::Capture::GraphicsCaptureAccess::RequestAccessAsync(
                    winrt::Windows::Graphics::Capture::GraphicsCaptureAccessKind::Borderless).get());
            } catch (...) {
                answer->set_exception(std::current_exception());
            }
        }).detach();
        if (pending.wait_for(border_consent_timeout) != std::future_status::ready)
            return retained + "Windows did not answer the consent request within 3 seconds.";
        const Status status = pending.get();
        if (status != Status::Allowed)
            return retained + "Windows answered " + access_name(status) + " to the consent request.";
        session.IsBorderRequired(false);
        return "";
    } catch (const winrt::hresult_error& error) {
        return retained + "consent request failed: " + winrt::to_string(error.message()) + ".";
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        return retained + "consent request failed: " + error.what() + ".";
    }
}
} // namespace

void Session::capture(std::stop_token stop, std::promise<void> ready) {
    bool signaled = false;
    namespace Capture = winrt::Windows::Graphics::Capture;
    namespace GraphicsDirectX = winrt::Windows::Graphics::DirectX;
    Capture::Direct3D11CaptureFramePool pool{nullptr};
    Capture::GraphicsCaptureSession capture_session{nullptr};
    std::unique_ptr<Apartment> apartment;
    try {
        apartment = std::make_unique<Apartment>();
        if (!Capture::GraphicsCaptureSession::IsSupported()) throw std::runtime_error("Windows Graphics Capture is not supported on this session.");
        HWND window = reinterpret_cast<HWND>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(config.window));
        HMONITOR monitor = window ? MonitorFromWindow(window, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST)
            : reinterpret_cast<HMONITOR>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(config.monitor));
        if (!monitor) monitor = MonitorFromPoint(POINT{0, 0}, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY);
        if (window && !IsWindow(window)) throw std::runtime_error("Game window is no longer available.");
        d3d = std::make_unique<D3D>(monitor, config.gpu_device);
        auto interop = winrt::get_activation_factory<Capture::GraphicsCaptureItem, IGraphicsCaptureItemInterop>();
        Capture::GraphicsCaptureItem item{nullptr};
        if (window) check(interop->CreateForWindow(window, winrt::guid_of<Capture::GraphicsCaptureItem>(), winrt::put_abi(item)));
        else check(interop->CreateForMonitor(monitor, winrt::guid_of<Capture::GraphicsCaptureItem>(), winrt::put_abi(item)));
        auto size = item.Size();
        if (size.Width < 2 || size.Height < 2) throw std::runtime_error("Capture target has no visible content.");
        fit_output(config, size.Width, size.Height);
        validate(config);
        if (d3d->requested_fallback)
            log(1, "Selected GPU \"" + utf8(gpu_id) + "\" is unavailable; using " + utf8(d3d->name) + ".");
        auto callback = [this](int stream, const AVPacket* packet, AVRational base) { emit(stream, packet, base); };
        log(0, "Initializing GPU capture: " + utf8(d3d->name) + " / " + std::to_string(config.width)
            + "x" + std::to_string(config.height) + " / " + std::to_string(config.fps) + " FPS.");
        video = std::make_unique<VideoEncoder>(*d3d, config, callback);
        description = video->description;
        ComPtr<IDXGIDevice> dxgi; check(d3d->device.As(&dxgi));
        winrt::com_ptr<IInspectable> inspectable;
        check(CreateDirect3D11DeviceFromDXGIDevice(dxgi.Get(), inspectable.put()));
        auto device = inspectable.as<GraphicsDirectX::Direct3D11::IDirect3DDevice>();
        pool = Capture::Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::CreateFreeThreaded(device,
            GraphicsDirectX::DirectXPixelFormat::B8G8R8A8UIntNormalized, 3, size);
        capture_session = pool.CreateCaptureSession(item);
        capture_session.IsCursorCaptureEnabled(false);
        const std::string border = request_borderless(capture_session);
        auto closed = std::make_shared<std::atomic<bool>>(false);
        auto closed_handler = item.Closed(winrt::auto_revoke, [closed](auto&&, auto&&) { *closed = true; });
        epoch_100ns = qpc_100ns();
        audio = std::make_unique<AudioCapture>(config, epoch_100ns, callback,
            [this](std::string message) { log(2, message); failed = true; },
            [this](std::string message) { log(1, message); });
        // Audio parameters are final now; video parameters are frozen on the first packet.
        for (AVCodecContext* codec : {video->codec.get()}) {
            auto* p = avcodec_parameters_alloc(); if (!p) throw std::bad_alloc();
            headers.emplace_back(p); avcheck(avcodec_parameters_from_context(p, codec), "Copy video codec headers");
        }
        for (const auto& codec : audio->codecs) {
            auto* p = avcodec_parameters_alloc(); if (!p) throw std::bad_alloc();
            headers.emplace_back(p); avcheck(avcodec_parameters_from_context(p, codec.get()), "Copy AAC headers");
        }
        audio->start();
        capture_session.StartCapture();
        running = true; ready.set_value(); signaled = true;
        log(0, "WGC + D3D11 NV12 + " + utf8(description) + " + WASAPI started. SDR capture." + (border.empty() ? "" : " " + border));
        ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> last_texture;
        int input_width = 0, input_height = 0;
        int64_t last_pts = -1;
        int64_t last_arrival = epoch_100ns;
        PreciseTimer pacer;
        auto next = Clock::now();
        const auto interval = std::chrono::nanoseconds(1'000'000'000 / config.fps);
        while (!stop.stop_requested() && !failed && !closed->load()) {
            next += interval;
            for (int attempts = 0; attempts < 3; ++attempts) {
                auto frame = pool.TryGetNextFrame();
                if (!frame) break;
                auto actual = frame.ContentSize();
                if (actual.Width < 2 || actual.Height < 2) { frame.Close(); continue; }
                auto surface = frame.Surface().as<::Windows::Graphics::DirectX::Direct3D11::IDirect3DDxgiInterfaceAccess>();
                ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture;
                check(surface->GetInterface(IID_PPV_ARGS(&texture)));
                D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC desc{}; texture->GetDesc(&desc);
                if (actual.Width <= static_cast<int>(desc.Width) && actual.Height <= static_cast<int>(desc.Height)) {
                    if (input_width != actual.Width || input_height != actual.Height) {
                        D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC owned{};
                        owned.Width = actual.Width; owned.Height = actual.Height;
                        owned.MipLevels = 1; owned.ArraySize = 1; owned.Format = DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM;
                        owned.SampleDesc.Count = 1; owned.BindFlags = D3D11_BIND_RENDER_TARGET;
                        last_texture.Reset(); check(d3d->device->CreateTexture2D(&owned, nullptr, &last_texture));
                        input_width = actual.Width; input_height = actual.Height;
                    }
                    D3D11_BOX box{0, 0, 0, static_cast<UINT>(input_width), static_cast<UINT>(input_height), 1};
                    d3d->context->CopySubresourceRegion(last_texture.Get(), 0, 0, 0, 0, texture.Get(), 0, &box);
                    last_arrival = qpc_100ns();
                }
                frame.Close();
                if (actual.Width != size.Width || actual.Height != size.Height) {
                    size = actual; pool.Recreate(device, GraphicsDirectX::DirectXPixelFormat::B8G8R8A8UIntNormalized, 3, size);
                    break;
                }
            }
            auto now = qpc_100ns();
            stale = now - last_arrival > 20'000'000;
            if (last_texture) {
                int64_t pts = av_rescale(now - epoch_100ns, config.fps, 10'000'000);
                if (pts > last_pts) {
                    if (last_pts >= 0) dropped += std::max<int64_t>(0, pts - last_pts - 1);
                    video->encode(last_texture.Get(), input_width, input_height, pts);
                    last_pts = pts; ++frames_count;
                }
            } else if (now - epoch_100ns > 50'000'000) {
                throw std::runtime_error("WGC returned no frames for 5 seconds. Restore the window / disable protected or exclusive presentation.");
            }
            if (next < Clock::now() - interval) next = Clock::now();
            pacer.sleep_until(next);
        }
        if (closed->load()) log(1, "Capture target closed.");
        capture_session.Close(); capture_session = nullptr;
        pool.Close(); pool = nullptr;
        audio->stop(); video->drain(true);
    } catch (const winrt::hresult_error& e) {
        failed = true;
        if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception());
        else log(2, "Capture: " + winrt::to_string(e.message()));
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        failed = true;
        if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception()); else log(2, e.what());
    } catch (...) {
        failed = true;
        if (!signaled) ready.set_exception(std::current_exception()); else log(2, "Unknown capture error");
    }
    // Never let an exception escape a worker or a C ABI callback.
    if (audio) audio->stop();
    try { if (capture_session) capture_session.Close(); if (pool) pool.Close(); } catch (...) { }
    running = false;
}
}

inline void avcheck(int code, const char* operation) {
    if (code >= 0) return;
    char message[AV_ERROR_MAX_STRING_SIZE]{};
    av_strerror(code, message, sizeof(message));
    throw std::runtime_error(std::string(operation) + ": " + message + (ffmpeg_detail.empty() ? "" : " / " + ffmpeg_detail));
}
inline int64_t qpc_100ns() {
    LARGE_INTEGER value, frequency;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&value); QueryPerformanceFrequency(&frequency);
    return av_rescale(value.QuadPart, 10'000'000, frequency.QuadPart);
}
inline std::string utf8(const std::wstring& value) { return winrt::to_string(value); }

struct FrameDelete { void operator()(AVFrame* p) const { av_frame_free(&p); } };
struct PacketDelete { void operator()(AVPacket* p) const { av_packet_free(&p); } };

struct Handle {
    HANDLE value = nullptr;
    explicit Handle(HANDLE value = nullptr) : value(value) {}
    ~Handle() { if (value && value != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(value); }
    Handle(const Handle&) = delete;
    Handle& operator=(const Handle&) = delete;
};
struct Apartment {
    HRESULT result = RoInitialize(RO_INIT_MULTITHREADED);
    Apartment() { if (FAILED(result) && result != RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE) check(result); }
    ~Apartment() { if (SUCCEEDED(result)) RoUninitialize(); }
};
// Frame pacing at 60/120 FPS needs sub-millisecond wakeups. std::this_thread::sleep_* rides the system timer
// (~15.6 ms by default), which makes a 16.7 ms loop wake late and skip or repeat frames. A high-resolution
// waitable timer (Windows 10 1803+) wakes on time without raising the global timer resolution.
class PreciseTimer {
    Handle timer{CreateWaitableTimerExW(nullptr, nullptr, CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS)};
public:
    template <class Rep, class Period>
    void sleep_for(std::chrono::duration<Rep, Period> duration) {
        auto ticks = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<int64_t, std::ratio<1, 10'000'000>>>(duration).count();
        if (ticks <= 0) return;
        LARGE_INTEGER due{}; due.QuadPart = -ticks; // Negative: relative, in 100 ns units.
        if (timer.value && SetWaitableTimer(timer.value, &due, 0, nullptr, nullptr, FALSE) &&
            WaitForSingleObject(timer.value, INFINITE) == WAIT_OBJECT_0) return;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(duration); // Older Windows or a failed timer: coarse but correct.
    }
    void sleep_until(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point deadline) {
        sleep_for(deadline - std::chrono::steady_clock::now());
    }
};

using Emit = std::function<void(int, const AVPacket*, AVRational)>;
